examples.ko: 아버지는 창고에 공구를 많이 두고 계세요.
examples.en: My father keeps many tools in the storage room.
I could not fix the chair because I had no tools.
This shop sells only tools.
Please take the screwdriver out of the toolbox.

examples.ko: 자전거를 고칠 때는 간단한 공구면 충분해요.
examples.en: Simple tools are enough for fixing a bike.

examples.ko: 이 공구는 쓴 뒤에 꼭 닦아야 해요.
examples.en: You must wipe this tool after using it.

explain: 철물점이나 공구 가게에서 사는 망치, 드라이버, 렌치 같은 연장을 말해요. '도구'는 펜이나 책까지 넓게 가리키고, 공구는 수리와 공사에 쓰는 도구예요. 인터넷에서는 '공동구매'를 줄여 '공구'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It covers hammers, screwdrivers and wrenches that you buy at a hardware store. 도구 is wider and can include pens or books, while 공구 is for repairs and construction. Online, '공구' is also short for '공동구매' (group buying).

examples.en: Grandmother put the wild greens in a basket.
She carries a basket on her head to the market.
I picked a basketful of apples.
This basket is made of bamboo.
I took a piece of bread out of the basket.
The basket was too heavy, so we lifted it together.

explain: 대나무나 싸리 같은 것으로 엮은 둥글고 큰 바구니예요. 요즘 일상에서는 보통 '바구니'라고 하고, '광주리'는 옛날 시장이나 시골 장면에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a large round basket woven from bamboo or similar material. In daily life today people usually say '바구니', while '광주리' often appears in scenes of old markets or the countryside.

examples.en: I spread a mat on the floor and sat down.
The mat is thin, so the floor feels cold.

examples.ko: 강아지 집에 부드러운 깔개를 넣어 줬어요.
examples.en: I put a soft pad in the dog's house.
I did yoga on this mat.

examples.ko: 이 깔개는 세탁기로 빨 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can wash this mat in the washing machine.
I bought a new cushion pad for the chair.

explain: 바닥이나 의자 위에 까는 물건을 두루 가리키는 말이에요. 방석, 돗자리, 매트는 각각 이름이 따로 있고, '깔개'는 그 모두를 넓게 부를 때 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a broad word for things laid on a floor or on a chair. Cushions, picnic mats and exercise mats each have their own names, and '깔개' can be used to refer to all of them in general.

examples.en: I got angry and crumpled up the letter.

examples.ko: 다 쓴 종이를 꾸겨서 쓰레기통에 던졌어요.
examples.en: I crumpled the used paper and threw it into the trash can.
I wrinkled all my clothes while stuffing them into the bag.
Don't crumple the receipt; keep it flat.
My younger sibling crumpled my test paper and ran away.

examples.ko: 옷을 꾸기면 다림질해도 잘 안 펴져요.
examples.en: If you crumple clothes, they don't smooth out well even when ironed.

explain: 종이나 옷을 주름이 생기게 구기는 동작이에요. 보통 '구기다'라고 하고, '꾸기다'는 그보다 센 느낌의 말이에요. 저절로 주름이 생긴 상태는 '꾸겨지다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the action of crumpling paper or clothes so they get creases. People usually say '구기다', and '꾸기다' is a stronger-sounding form of it. For something that becomes wrinkled by itself, say '꾸겨지다'.

examples.en: I put the shelf up on a fairly high part of the wall.

examples.ko: 언덕 위에 높직하게 지은 집이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a house built fairly high up on the hill.
The seat of this chair is rather high.

examples.ko: 창문이 높직해서 밖이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The window is rather high, so I can't see outside well.

examples.ko: 그 담이 높직하다고 들었는데 생각보다 낮네요.
examples.en: I heard that wall was rather high, but it's lower than I thought.

examples.ko: 높직해 보이는 담장 너머로 감나무가 보였어요.
examples.en: I could see a persimmon tree over the fence that looked rather high.

explain: '높다'보다 부드럽고 '꽤 높은 편이다'라는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '꽤 높다'라고 많이 말하고, 높직하다는 글이나 묘사에서 더 잘 보여요.
explain_en: It is softer than '높다' and feels like 'fairly high'. In daily talk people often just say '꽤 높다', while 높직하다 appears more in writing and descriptions.

examples.ko: 대학 때는 친척 집에서 더부살이를 했어요.
examples.en: In college, I lived as a dependent at a relative's house.
Living off a friend's home wasn't all comfortable.

examples.ko: 서울에 처음 올라와서 형 집에 더부살이로 지냈어요.
examples.en: When I first came up to Seoul, I stayed at my older brother's place as a dependent.
Since I'm living at someone else's place, I'm always careful about what others think.

examples.ko: 더부살이 신세를 벗어나려고 열심히 돈을 모았어요.
examples.en: I saved money hard to get out of living off others.

examples.ko: 아버지는 젊을 때 했던 더부살이 이야기를 가끔 해 주세요.
examples.en: My father sometimes tells me stories about the time he lived in someone else's house when he was young.

explain: 남의 집에서 신세를 지고 사는 느낌이 있어서, 월세를 내고 사는 '하숙'과는 달라요. '더부살이 신세'처럼 불편하고 눈치 보이는 처지를 말할 때도 써요. '얹혀살다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of living at someone else's home as a dependent, which is different from paying rent in a boarding house ('하숙'). It also appears in '더부살이 신세' for an uncomfortable position where you have to watch others' reactions. People also say '얹혀살다'.

examples.en: Looking at the vast sea refreshes my mind.

examples.ko: 제주도에 가면 드넓은 초원을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to Jeju Island, you can see vast grasslands.

examples.ko: 방학 때 드넓은 들판에서 자전거를 탔어요.
examples.en: During vacation I rode a bicycle in a vast field.

examples.ko: 이 공원은 정말 드넓어서 하루 종일 걸어도 다 못 봐요.
examples.en: This park is so vast that you can't see all of it even if you walk all day.

examples.ko: 드넓게 펼쳐진 하늘 아래에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took photos under the sky stretching out wide.
The children run freely around the huge playground.

explain: '넓다'에 '드-'가 붙어서 매우 넓다는 느낌을 강조해요. 바다, 들판, 하늘, 초원처럼 눈앞에 크게 펼쳐진 풍경에 잘 어울리고, 방이나 책상처럼 작은 것에는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: The prefix '드-' on '넓다' adds the feeling of being very wide. It suits scenery spread out before your eyes, such as the sea, fields, sky and grasslands, and is rarely used for small things like a room or desk.

examples.ko: 구멍 난 양동이를 땜질해서 다시 썼어요.
examples.en: I patched the bucket with a hole and used it again.

examples.ko: 급하게 땜질해 봤자 금방 또 터져요.
examples.en: Even if you patch it in a hurry, it will burst again soon.

examples.ko: 아저씨가 깨진 냄비 바닥을 땜질해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The man soldered the cracked bottom of the pot for me.
You shouldn't handle the problem by just patching it up.
Let's patch it for now and fix it properly later.

examples.ko: 예산이 없어서 낡은 시설을 땜질하는 데 그쳤어요.
examples.en: With no budget, they only managed to patch up the old facilities.

explain: 금속을 때우는 일이지만 일상에서는 '임시로 대충 고치다'라는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. '고치다'는 제대로 고치는 느낌이고, '땜질하다'는 급한 부분만 막는다는 느낌이 있어요. '땜질하듯', '땜질해서'처럼 이어서 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It literally means to solder metal, but in daily life it is more often used for fixing something temporarily and roughly. '고치다' feels like a proper repair, while '땜질하다' suggests only plugging the urgent spot. It is often used in forms like '땜질하듯' and '땜질해서'.

examples.en: I tripped on the threshold and almost fell.
The baby couldn't get over the threshold and cried.
The sill is high, so wheelchairs can't get in.
Please take off your shoes before the threshold.
He sat on the threshold and tied his shoelaces.
It feels like we've stepped onto the edge of winter.

explain: '턱'은 계단이나 길의 높이 차이를 넓게 가리키고, '문턱'은 문 바로 아래에만 써요. '문턱을 넘다'는 어떤 단계에 처음 들어선다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 병원은 문턱이 높아서 가기 어려워요.
phrases.en: hard to get into; intimidating to approach
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 기관에 들어가거나 이용하기가 부담스러울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a place or institution feels hard or intimidating to enter or use.

explain_en: '턱' is any small step in height on a path or stairs, while '문턱' is only the one right under a door. '문턱을 넘다' can also mean stepping into a new stage.

examples.en: A ball of thread came out of the drawer.
I threw a wad of paper into the trash can.
The cat threw up a hairball.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 서류 뭉치가 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: A pile of documents is stacked on the desk.

examples.ko: 눈을 한 뭉치 굴려서 눈사람을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I rolled a lump of snow and made a snowman.

examples.ko: 돈 뭉치를 들고 있는 사람을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a person holding a wad of money.

explain: '뭉치'는 여러 개가 한데 엉기거나 묶여 덩어리가 된 것이에요. 혼자 쓰기보다 '실 뭉치', '종이 뭉치', '털 뭉치'처럼 앞에 재료를 붙여요. 동사 '뭉치다'와 같은 뿌리의 말이에요.
explain_en: 뭉치 is a lump or bundle formed when many things get tangled or tied together. It usually comes after a material, as in '실 뭉치' or '털 뭉치'. It shares its root with the verb '뭉치다'.

examples.ko: 연필 끝이 뭉툭해서 잘 안 써져요.
examples.en: The pencil tip is blunt, so it doesn't write well.
My fingertips are stubby and short.

examples.ko: 뭉툭한 칼로는 야채가 잘 안 썰려요.
examples.en: Vegetables don't cut well with a dull knife.
I often hear that the tip of my nose is rounded.
If the toe of the shoe is rounded, your feet are comfortable.
Scissors for kids are made with blunt tips.

explain: 끝이 뾰족하지 않고 두툼하고 무딘 모양을 말해요. 반대말은 '뾰족하다'나 '날카롭다'예요. '무디다'는 날이 잘 안 드는 것에 쓰고, '뭉툭하다'는 끝의 생김새에 쓴다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes a shape whose end is thick and blunt rather than pointed. Its opposites are '뾰족하다' and '날카롭다'. '무디다' is for things whose edge doesn't cut well, while '뭉툭하다' is about the shape of the tip.

examples.en: I put fruit in the shopping basket.
I picked up a basket at the entrance of the mart.
The basket is full, so it's heavy.
I put sandwiches and drinks in the picnic basket.

examples.ko: 예쁜 바스켓은 꽃을 꽂아 두기에도 좋아요.
examples.en: A pretty basket is also nice for holding flowers.

examples.ko: 저는 빨래 바스켓을 방 한쪽에 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put the laundry basket in a corner of the room.

explain: '바스켓'은 영어 basket에서 온 말이지만 한국어에서는 '바구니'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '바스켓'은 '쇼핑 바스켓', '피크닉 바스켓'처럼 외래어 이름에 붙어서 더 자주 보여요. 일상에서는 '바구니'라고 하면 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 바스켓 comes from English 'basket', but Koreans use 바구니 far more often. You mostly see 바스켓 in loan-style names such as 쇼핑 바스켓 or 피크닉 바스켓. In daily speech, 바구니 sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 호텔 로비에 큰 샹들리에가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A large chandelier hangs in the hotel lobby.

examples.ko: 밤이 되자 샹들리에 불빛이 반짝반짝 빛나요.
examples.en: When night falls, the chandelier lights sparkle.
You need a ladder to clean the chandelier.
We took a photo under the big chandelier.

examples.ko: 우리 집 거실에 작은 샹들리에를 달았어요.
examples.en: We hung a small chandelier in our living room.
This chandelier is made from pieces of glass.

explain: 프랑스어에서 온 외래어로, 여러 개의 전구나 유리 장식이 달린 화려한 천장 조명을 말해요. 평범한 천장 등은 '전등'이나 '조명'이라고 해서 구별해요. 호텔, 극장, 결혼식장 같은 곳에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: This loanword from French refers to a fancy ceiling light with many bulbs or glass decorations. Ordinary ceiling lights are called '전등' or '조명', so the two are kept apart. You often see chandeliers in hotels, theaters and wedding halls.

examples.en: I adopted a pet cat.
This animal is easy to keep as a pet.
I went to the mart to buy pet food.
A pet turtle definitely needs a tank.
I bought a toy at the pet supplies store.

examples.ko: 애완용 물고기 먹이를 하루에 한 번 줘요.
examples.en: I feed my pet fish once a day.

explain: '애완용 고양이', '애완용으로 키우다'처럼 뒤에 명사가 오거나 '으로'가 붙어 써요. 요즘은 가족으로 생각하는 마음을 담아 '반려동물', '반려견'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 사람이 아닌 동물에 대해 말하고 물건을 소개할 때는 '애완용품'이라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: It is used before a noun or with '으로', as in '애완용 고양이' and '애완용으로 키우다'. These days people also often say '반려동물' or '반려견' to show they think of the animal as family. For products you also see the word '애완용품' (pet supplies).

examples.ko: 안 쓰는 물건을 창고에 처박아 뒀어요.
examples.en: I shoved the things I don't use into the storeroom.
I stuffed the old luggage into a corner of the closet.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 가방을 방구석에 처박고 나갔어요.
examples.en: I was angry, so I flung my bag into the corner of the room and went out.

examples.ko: 책을 서랍에 처박지 말고 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just shove the book in a drawer; try reading it.
There was an accident where a car slammed into a wall.

examples.ko: 쓰지도 않는 물건을 계속 처박으면 집이 좁아져요.
examples.en: If you keep stuffing away things you don't even use, your home gets cramped.

explain: '넣다', '두다'보다 거칠고 함부로 하는 느낌이 있어요. 안 쓰는 물건을 아무 데나 밀어 둘 때, 또는 차를 세게 박을 때 써요. 피동형 '처박히다'는 '방에만 처박혀 있다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It feels rougher and more careless than '넣다' or '두다'. It is used when shoving unused things anywhere, or when a car crashes hard into something. The passive '처박히다' is used like '방에만 처박혀 있다' (stay holed up in a room).

examples.en: I spent a night in a log cabin in the mountains with friends.
I like log cabins because they smell of wood.
We rented a log cabin and spent our summer vacation there.
Smoke is coming from the log cabin's chimney.
There is a small log cabin by the lake.

examples.ko: 통나무집에 가면 장작불을 피워 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: If I go to a log cabin, I want to try making a wood fire.

explain: 통나무로 지은 집이라서 산이나 호수 근처에서 놀러 갈 때 이야기하는 숙소로 많이 나와요. '통나무'는 가공하지 않은 굵은 나무 몸통이에요.
explain_en: Since it is a house built from logs, it often comes up as a place to stay on trips near mountains or lakes. '통나무' means an unprocessed thick tree trunk.

examples.en: The hotel lobby was really luxurious.

examples.ko: 호화로운 결혼식에 손님이 아주 많이 왔어요.
examples.en: A great many guests came to the lavish wedding.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 젊을 때 호화롭게 살았어요.
examples.en: That couple lived in luxury when they were young.

examples.ko: 호화로워 보이는 저택 앞에 차가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A car is parked in front of the luxurious-looking mansion.
The room was so lavish that it was rather uncomfortable.
A gift does not have to be lavish.

explain: 돈을 아주 많이 써서 화려하고 비싸 보이는 모습이에요. 칭찬일 때도 있지만 조금 지나치다는 느낌이 들어갈 때가 많아요. '화려하다'는 눈에 띄게 예쁘다는 쪽이고, 호화롭다는 돈이 많이 들었다는 쪽이에요. 같은 말로 '호화스럽다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes something that looks glamorous and expensive because a lot of money was spent. It can be admiring, but often carries a feeling of excess. '화려하다' is about being eye-catching and pretty, while 호화롭다 is about money having been spent. '호화스럽다' has the same meaning.
